implemented.summary: Conchbase owns the agent loop, Agent identities/revisions, task state, durable work, permissions, and private SQLite state.

The exact 47-path local-first 1.0.0 platform is implemented, including authentication metadata, work control, recovery, one local Source, capability records, and process-scoped write-only SecretHandles.
Architecture, documentation, and validation are optimized for AI coding agents; human handoff is not a product requirement.
Pagurus implements the paired 1.0.0 control client through published Runtime routes and capability gates.

The Organization Runtime product loop is implemented under ADR 0041: one primary conversation, dynamic Agent revisions, Delegations, concurrent work, structured reports, Attention, archive/offboard/resume, and published 1.1.0 client state.
The complete local-first Boss-mode Organization Runtime loop is implemented and validated with a dual-repository fake-provider fixture.

ADR 0038 fixes the additive 1.1.0 organization API shape and ADR 0041 corrects the published session, optional discovery, intent identity, errors, and execution semantics; Pagurus consumes these through its paired typed client.

A pure internal organization kernel validates structured actions, state transitions, bounded delegation, structured reports, attention decisions, and archive/offboard/resume events without public API or persistence changes.
An internal in-memory organization store holds one primary snapshot, applies validated actions, and exposes bounded event reads without becoming a persistence owner or public API.

An internal SQLite organization store shares Conchbase's single database owner, persists validated bounded actions in the private schema, and replays one coherent snapshot after restart without public API changes; ADR 0050 keeps the current private schema at user_version 5 with Agent Chat tables.
A pure internal planner enforces bounded launches, attention priority, structured relays, and work-control command boundaries without executing work, calling a model, or changing the public API.
A pure internal projection converts an accepted create_agent action into a deterministic digest-only proposal without creating an Agent revision, granting capability, or changing the public API.

An internal Runtime-service coordinator commits organization actions, derives execution plans, and dispatches only injected published work controls without HTTP routes, model calls, tool calls, or Agent revision writes.

An additive 1.1.0 organization API exposes 18 published-state paths with intent idempotency, attention answer/withdraw versions, bounded event cursors, and no drafts, transcripts, plaintext, private files, or locally computed authority.

A Runtime-owned Boss-mode bridge parses untrusted structured intent output, commits validated actions, creates real Agent revisions through TaskService, binds durable WorkItems, and returns ordered structured relays.

CONCHBASE_ORGANIZATION_INTENT_MODEL enables an optional OpenAI-compatible structured parser for the primary conversation while preserving authoritative action validation and offline deterministic fallback.

Dynamic worker proposals are bridged through the existing Agent profile boundary into immutable, model-validated Agent revisions; digests never become instructions and proposals never grant authority.
Authorized organization workers bind to accepted durable WorkItems and bounded work controls through the existing execution substrate.
Parent/child Delegation actions remain topology-neutral and are enforced by scope/capability subset, recursion depth, TTL, and revival/revalidation rules.
Structured reports, attention requests, blocked/failed facts, and completion events are validated organization facts and enter primary relays in deterministic order.
Project quiet/archive/offboard/resume transitions preserve events, revoke active authority, and require revalidation before resumed projects accept new work.
ADR 0043 implements deterministic controlled execution v1 with explicit grants, request approval/rejection, digest-only fake execution, revocation, and bounded audit events over additive 1.2.0 paths.

ADR 0044 implements isolated local execution v2 with a fixed Node child-process worker, closed deterministic operations, durable queued/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled/interrupted runs, explicit start/cancel/recover, restart interruption, and digest-only audit over additive 1.3.0 paths.

ADR 0045 implements an additive 1.4.0 primary-conversation read model over Runtime-owned organization facts, with bounded user messages, Boss acknowledgements, worker activity, reports, Attention, system status, cursors, and no raw transcripts or private state.
ADR 0046 implements an additive 1.5.0 Agent Chat module that reuses configured Agent revisions and Agent-backed tasks over the user-configured Magpie OpenAI-compatible protocol endpoint.
ADR 0047 exposes Boss Mode as a Runtime-owned virtual 老板 Agent inside Agent Chat, routing messages through BossModeService while preserving Runtime authority and one primary conversation.
ADR 0048 implements a Runtime-published Agent Chat conversation state model with thinking, streaming, organizing, waiting_attention, replied, failed, unavailable, and cancelled states.

ADR 0049 implements natural Boss Agent conversation through the user-configured OpenAI-compatible protocol endpoint, with bounded context, optional Runtime-adjudicated actions, and no new public path or schema.

ADR 0050 separates pure Boss chat from organization execution, projects readable organization facts and capability boundaries, streams provider progress, persists Agent Chat under private user_version 5, and recovers in-flight messages on restart.
ADR 0051 adds optional provider-neutral model selection at Agent Chat conversation creation, validated against the Magpie catalog and pinned for ordinary Agent and Boss conversation turns.

ADR 0052 accepts a Runtime-owned bounded Agent loop, capability-provider seam, explicit approval state, durable per-iteration events, and bounded multi-turn provider context without changing Runtime authority.

ADR 0053 implements a Runtime-owned bounded Agent loop for Agent-backed tasks with read-only built-in tools (workspace_list, workspace_read, text_search), multi-turn provider context, durable agent_loop events, iteration and time budgets, and path-escape rejection.

ADR 0054 implements an administrator-configured MCP stdio provider without the MCP SDK: JSON-RPC handshake, tool allowlist, read-only enforcement, sanitized environment, timeouts, bounded results, and namespaced tool ids.
ADR 0055 adds GET /v1/agent-chat/conversations for recent conversation recovery, pins reasoningEffort per conversation, and exposes it to provider requests; private schema advances to user_version 6.

validationEvidence.summary: Both repositories run npm run check, npm test, and npm run build in CI.
An executable opt-in live loopback test covers two Agents, pinned revisions, configuration history, legacy tasks, cancellation, interruption, retry, and event replay.
A completed 54-request local loopback E2E walkthrough is documented as validation evidence, not as an executable repository fixture.
An executable credential-free local HTTP fixture covers catalog, non-streaming, streaming, observation, error, limit, and cancellation compatibility for the current adapter.
An executable portable-path fixture covers committed task/event recovery after abrupt process exit, additive migration preservation, one-owner rejection, and reopen after close.
An executable pure fixture covers project/worker/report/attention state machines, bounded delegation, archive/offboard/resume, secret-like rejection, and bounded events.
An executable fixture covers one organization snapshot, sequential action application, initialization, and bounded event reads.

An executable fixture covers private schema migration from user_version 3 to 4, action replay after reopen, stale sequence rejection, single-owner rejection, bounded persisted actions, and unchanged 47-path OpenAPI.
An executable fixture covers bounded concurrent launches, attention priority, structured relay order, work-control vocabulary, bounded values, and unchanged 47-path OpenAPI.
An executable fixture covers deterministic digest-only proposals, rejection of secret-like and non-organization actions, and absence of public routes or store writes.
An executable fixture covers action commit, stale rejection, injected work-control dispatch, callback failure recovery, and absence of HTTP/Agent/model/tool/public-route dependencies.

An executable fixture covers exact 65 OpenAPI paths, runtime discovery, 202 intents, idempotent replay/conflict, attention answer/withdraw and stale versions, event cursors and bounds, and no plaintext/private-state leakage.
Executable fixtures cover structured intent parsing, dynamic Agent revision creation, durable WorkItem binding, idempotent primary-conversation HTTP entry, and no plaintext/private-state leakage.
An executable HTTP fixture proves a primary-conversation intent creates published project/worker state and replays idempotently through the additive 1.1.0 API.
An executable fixture covers deterministic parsing, an OpenAI-compatible structured adapter, out-of-schema action rejection, and secret-like relay rejection.

A dual-repository live loopback fixture drives Pagurus typed organization clients over a credential-free fake provider through multiple projects, concurrent workers, one attention answer, and one archive/resume path.

An executable fixture covers explicit grants, stale versions, idempotency, approved fake execution, rejected requests, revocation, public paths, discovery, digest-only results, and no plaintext/private-path leakage.

An executable fixture covers approved-request/active-grant run creation, isolated child-process execution, stale versions, idempotency conflicts, cancel/recover, restart interruption, public run discovery, adapters, and no plaintext/private-path leakage.
An executable fixture covers ordered primary-conversation messages, bounded cursors, duplicate suppression, no private-state leakage, 1.4.0 discovery, and HTTP error paths.
An executable fixture covers configured Agent conversation creation, real Agent-backed model reply, idempotent replay, bounded errors, 1.5.0 discovery, and no private-state leakage.
An executable fixture covers virtual Boss Agent listing, conversation routing through BossModeService, bounded Runtime reply, organization session projection, and no normal Agent task creation.
An executable fixture covers normal Agent thinking/streaming/replied states and Runtime-owned conversation fields without private-state leakage.

An executable fixture covers natural Boss replies, optional organization action proposals, strict output rejection, unavailable classification, no fixed fallback phrase, and no normal Agent task creation.
Executable fixtures cover pure-chat no organization writes, readable organization facts, SSE progress, identity/capability normalization, durable Agent Chat reopen, and in-flight restart recovery.
Executable fixtures cover loop continuation after a tool result, iteration-budget termination, out-of-root rejection, read-only provider surface, and streamed tool-call accumulation.
Executable fixtures cover MCP discovery, namespacing, calls, non-read rejection, timeouts, malformed responses, bounded output, config validation, and Agent loop integration.
Executable fixtures cover conversation listing, default model selection, reasoning-effort pinning and validation, and history survival across restart.

blockedDirections.summary: Real MCP/Skill/plugin lifecycle, external Sources, external writes, arbitrary host tool execution, and crash-safe external side effects remain blocked; ADR 0044 implements only isolated local deterministic operations with no external write.
OS-managed key custody, replayable encrypted-at-rest values, and production revocation.
External Sources, real Outbox writes, external side effects, and crash-safe reconciliation.
Real tool authorization, executor isolation, MCP lifecycle, Skill/plugin loading, and crash-safe side effects.
Production remote pairing UX, deployment validation, hardened token lifecycle, and cloud deployment.
Generated client types built from a separately accepted stable schema contract.

nextBoundedSlices.summary: Add a Skill directory provider that supplies instructions only and grants no capability.

invariants: Never expose SecretHandle plaintext to a model, client, event, log, error, configuration document, or generic resolver.
Never execute a tool outside the runtime policy and approval path.
Keep default binding loopback-only; non-loopback binding requires explicit approved pairing/authentication.
Do not let a UI read or write Conchbase private files or database.
Do not hardcode a canonical Agent topology; user-authored composition remains topology-neutral.
Distinguish implemented behavior from roadmap and validation evidence.
